questions.correct: in blue is a postmodifier; boy is the head.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: in blue is a postmodifier; boy is the head.

narration.text:
句子有长有短，先别数单词。把修饰和补充信息暂时放到一边，留下能撑住意思的部分，就是句子的骨架；不同骨架，就是不同的基本句型。<#0.8#>
Birds fly。<#0.8#>谁在飞？Birds。发生了什么？fly。说到这里意思已经完整，fly 后面不缺动作对象，所以骨架只有主语和谓语，叫主谓结构，简写为 SV。<#0.8#>
She can sing。<#0.8#>句子里虽然有 can 和 sing 两个动词形式，却不能算成两个谓语。can 表示“能”，sing 说出具体动作，两部分合起来才是完整的谓语动词组。主语仍是 She，骨架仍然是 SV。<#0.8#>
The boy in blue is running。<#0.8#>先找谁在跑，答案是 The boy。in blue 只是帮助我们认出“穿蓝衣服的那个男孩”，它在主语内部修饰 boy。is running 要合起来看，表示正在跑。暂时拿开 in blue，核心关系没有改变。<#0.8#>
判断基本句型时，先找到完整的谓语动词组；再问“谁怎么了”，以及谓语后面是否还必须补什么；最后把时间、地点、方式和名词旁的修饰信息暂时移开。剩下的必需成分，才决定句型。

lessons.title: Subject–verb: SV
lessons.meta: The action is complete without an object

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: cried needs no object or complement; The baby cried is complete, so the skeleton is SV.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: at noon adds time; The train arrived remains complete.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: live takes no object here; in Suzhou is a place adverbial.

rules: SV contains a subject and an intransitive predicate; no object or complement is required.
Optional time or place adverbials do not change an SV skeleton.
A prepositional phrase is not automatically an object merely because it follows a verb.

questions.question: Which pattern is “The baby cried”?
questions.correct: cried needs no object, so the skeleton is SV.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: cried needs no object, so the skeleton is SV.

questions.question: What is “at noon” in “The train arrived at noon”?
questions.correct: It tells when the train arrived, not what it acted on.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: It tells when the train arrived, not what it acted on.

questions.question: What is the skeleton of “My grandparents live in Suzhou”?
questions.correct: in Suzhou is a place adverbial.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: in Suzhou is a place adverbial.

narration.text:
The baby cried。<#0.7#>先看谁，The baby，也就是这个宝宝。再看他怎么了，cried，哭了。说到这里，意思已经完整：宝宝哭了。后面不需要再补“哭了谁”或者“哭了什么”。这种只有“谁，加上做了什么”的骨架，叫主谓结构，也就是 SV。<#0.8#>
再看 The train arrived at noon。<#0.7#>at noon 只告诉我们什么时候到。把这段时间信息暂时遮住，火车到达这件事仍然完整，所以 at noon 不会把主谓结构变成别的句型。<#0.8#>
My grandparents live in Suzhou 也是一样。<#0.6#>in Suzhou 补充爷爷奶奶住在哪里。就算暂时不说地点，“爷爷奶奶居住”这个核心意思也已经成立。而且地点前有介词 in，不能因为它放在动词后面，就把 Suzhou 当成宾语。
判断 SV，可以做两步。先找“谁”和“怎么了”；再把时间、地点、方式这些补充信息暂时遮住。如果剩下的意思已经站得住，而且动词后不需要一个对象，这个动词在这里就是不及物用法，句子骨架就是 SV。

lessons.title: Subject–linking verb–complement: SVC
lessons.meta: The complement identifies or describes the subject

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: is transfers no action to a doctor; it links Mia with the identity a doctor.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: tastes links soup to delicious rather than taking an object.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: turned marks a change of state and yellow describes the subject.

rules: A nominal subject complement identifies the subject, and the linking verb connects them.
A sense verb used as a linking verb takes a subject complement describing the subject.
A change-of-state linking verb takes a complement showing the subject’s resulting state.

questions.question: What is “a doctor” in “Mia is a doctor”?
questions.correct: a doctor identifies Mia.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: a doctor identifies Mia.

questions.question: Which pattern is “The soup tastes delicious”?
questions.correct: tastes is linking and delicious describes soup.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: tastes is linking and delicious describes soup.

questions.question: Who or what does “yellow” describe?
questions.correct: yellow is a subject complement describing the leaves.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: yellow is a subject complement describing the leaves.

narration.text:
Mia is a doctor。<#0.7#>这句话不是说 Mia 做了一个叫 is 的动作，而是在说 Mia 是谁。is 像一座桥，把 Mia 和 a doctor 连在一起。桥后面的 a doctor 说明 Mia 的身份。这样的骨架叫主系表，也就是 SVC。<#0.8#>
再看 The soup tastes delicious。<#0.7#>这里不是“汤正在品尝美味的东西”。真正的意思是，这个汤尝起来很美味。delicious 描写的是前面的 soup，tastes 仍然只负责把两边连起来。<#0.8#>
The leaves turned yellow 说的是树叶变黄了。<#0.6#>yellow 说明树叶变化后的样子，turned 在这里表示“变得”，所以它也是连接作用。
判断 SVC，不要一看到动词就找动作对象。先问后面的内容是在回答“主语是谁”还是“主语怎么样”。如果答案是，而且中间的动词只是在连接身份、状态或变化，这个动词就叫系动词，后面说明主语的部分叫表语，也叫主语补语。可以把句子理解成“主语，等于或呈现出，后面的身份和状态”。这条关系成立，骨架就是 SVC。

lessons.title: Subject–verb–object: SVO
lessons.meta: The action is directed at one object

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: opened directs the action at the window; the window is the direct object, giving SVO.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: music is not physically affected, but it is the content involved in enjoy and is still the object.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: understood is transitive and the question is its direct object.

rules: In SVO, a transitive predicate takes one object affected or involved in the action.
An object may denote a concrete thing or abstract content.
To identify SVO, confirm that the verb is transitive and directly governs the following nominal element.

questions.question: What is the object in “Leo opened the window”?
questions.correct: the window receives the action of opened.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: the window receives the action of opened.

questions.question: Which pattern is “We enjoy music”?
questions.correct: enjoy takes the object music.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: enjoy takes the object music.

questions.question: What is “the question” in “She understood the question”?
questions.correct: the question is the direct object of understood.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: the question is the direct object of understood.

narration.text:
有些动词说完以后，意思还没结束。Leo opened the window。<#0.6#>先找到动作 opened，再问：打开了什么？答案是 the window。如果没有这个对象，听者会自然追问。the window 是 opened 直接指向的东西，语法上叫直接宾语。整个骨架是主谓宾，也就是 SVO。<#0.8#>
宾语不一定真的被碰到。We enjoy music。<#0.6#>music 没有承受一个看得见的动作，但它是 enjoy 所指向的内容，所以仍然是宾语。She understood the question 也一样，理解的内容是 the question。<#0.8#>
这三个例句里，宾语都直接跟在动词后面，中间没有介词。判断时不能只看位置，还要确认它是不是动作、想法或感受直接指向的内容。
判断 SVO，先找到动词，再问：这个动作、想法或感受直接指向谁，或者什么？如果不说出这个对象，意思会明显缺一块，而且对象直接由动词带出，中间没有介词，它就是直接宾语。主语、动词、这一个宾语合起来，就是 SVO。

lessons.title: Subject–verb–indirect object–direct object: SVOO
lessons.meta: A recipient plus a thing
examples: I bought a gift for my mother.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: me is the recipient and a camera is the thing transferred.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: teach can take learner plus content directly: us is the indirect object and English the direct object.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: for my mother is a prepositional phrase; compare I bought my mother a gift.

rules: SVOO commonly contains a recipient indirect object and a thing direct object.
Only certain verbs allow SVOO, such as give, send, show, teach, tell and buy.
A direct object plus a to/for phrase may resemble SVOO in meaning but differs structurally.

questions.question: What is “me” in “Dad gave me a camera”?
questions.correct: me is the recipient of the camera.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: me is the recipient of the camera.

questions.question: What is “English” in “She taught us English”?
questions.correct: English is the content taught.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: English is the content taught.

questions.question: What is “for my mother” in “I bought a gift for my mother”?
questions.correct: It is introduced by for, so it is not a bare indirect object.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: It is introduced by for, so it is not a bare indirect object.

narration.text:
Dad gave me a camera。<#0.7#>先别急着数动词后有几个词，先看发生了什么：爸爸给出一台相机，相机到了我这里。给的是什么？a camera。给了谁？me。一个是被传递的东西，一个是接收的人，所以句子有两个宾语，骨架叫主谓双宾，也就是 SVOO。<#0.8#>
在这个结构里，a camera 是动作直接涉及的东西，叫直接宾语；me 是接收者，叫间接宾语。虽然 me 排在前面，但“间接”和“直接”不是按前后顺序随便命名，而是看它们和动作的关系。<#0.8#>
She taught us English 也能这样看。教的内容是 English，学习这些内容的人是 us。
再看 I bought a gift for my mother。<#0.6#>这里 a gift 是直接宾语，for my mother 前面有 for，是一个介词短语。它仍然说明受益的人，却不是无介词连接的间接宾语，所以这句不算双宾结构。
判断 SVOO，就问两个问题：传递的是什么？接收者是谁？如果动词能够直接带出“接收者，加上事物或内容”，没有 to 或 for 隔开，这通常就是双宾结构。

lessons.title: Subject–verb–object–complement: SVOC
lessons.meta: The complement identifies, describes or completes the object
examples: I saw the bird fly away.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: captain identifies what Amy was elected to be.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: happy describes the state of the object him.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: fly away tells what the bird did.

rules: In SVOC, an object complement follows and says something about the object.
A noun or adjective can be an object complement of identity or state.
A non-finite verb can complement the object by showing its action or experience.

questions.question: What is “captain” in “They elected Amy captain”?
questions.correct: captain identifies Amy’s new role.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: captain identifies Amy’s new role.

questions.question: Which item is the object in “The news made him happy”?
questions.correct: him is the object and happy its complement.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: him is the object and happy its complement.

questions.question: Which skeleton fits “I saw the bird fly away”?
questions.correct: fly away complements bird by describing its action.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: fly away complements bird by describing its action.

narration.text:
They elected Amy captain。<#0.7#>动作指向 Amy，所以 Amy 是宾语。可句子还想告诉我们：Amy 被选成了什么？答案是 captain。captain 不是第二个被选出来的东西，而是在说明 Amy 的新身份。这样的骨架叫主谓宾补，也就是 SVOC。<#0.8#>
再看 The news made him happy。<#0.7#>him 是消息影响的人，happy 说明他后来是什么状态。him 和 happy 之间可以理解成“他变得开心”。后面的 happy 就是在补充说明宾语。<#0.8#>
I saw the bird fly away 也是同一条关系。<#0.6#>看到的是 the bird，而 fly away 告诉我们鸟做了什么。这里不是两个宾语。
最容易混的是把最后两部分都当成宾语。其实这里的后半部分不是另一个对象，而是在补充宾语的身份、状态或动作。两部分之间有说明与被说明的关系。<#0.8#>
判断 SVOC，可以把宾语和最后一部分看成一组小关系：最后一部分是否在说明这个宾语是谁、怎么样或做了什么？如果是，它就叫宾语补语，整个骨架就是 SVOC。

lessons.title: Existential there be
lessons.meta: Introducing the existence of someone or something
examples: There is a book on the desk.
There seems to be a problem.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: there introduces existence, while a book is the notional subject; Chinese commonly puts the place before an existential verb and the thing.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The notional subject two students is plural, so the verb is are; outside only gives the location.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Existential clauses can also use expressions such as seem to be.

rules: In an existential clause, there is an introductory dummy element and the following noun phrase is the notional subject.
The form of be normally agrees with the following noun phrase.
there be is a special existential construction, not an ordinary SVC pattern.

questions.question: What is the notional subject in “There is a book on the desk”?
questions.correct: a book is the entity whose existence is introduced.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: a book is the entity whose existence is introduced.

questions.question: There ___ two students outside.
questions.correct: be agrees with plural two students.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: be agrees with plural two students.

questions.question: How should “There seems to be a problem” be classified?
questions.correct: there introduces the existence of a problem.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: there introduces the existence of a problem.

narration.text: 走进一间屋子，想告诉别人桌上有一本书，英语会先把“有东西存在”这件事引出来。<#0.5#>There is a book on the desk。<#0.8#>开头的 There 不是“那里”的地点意思，它像一个开场提示：接下来要出现某样东西。真正被介绍出来的是 a book，所以它才是实义主语；on the desk 只补充书在哪里。<#0.8#>再看 There are two students outside。<#0.6#>这次出现的是 two students，数量是复数，因此前面的 be 动词用 are。outside 告诉我们人在什么地方，不负责决定单复数。判断时不要让最前面的 There 迷惑，要把目光移到 be 后面的名词短语。<#0.8#>There seems to be a problem 又多了一层语气。<#0.6#>它不是直接断定“有问题”，而是说“似乎有一个问题”。可见存在句不只会出现 is 或 are，也能用 seems to be 表达说话人的判断。<#0.8#>这类句子可以抓住三步：先认出 There 只是引出存在；再找 be 后真正出现的人或物；最后把地点放回去。中文常把地点放前面说“某处有某物”，英语则先用 There 打开这个存在画面。

lessons.title: Patterns with obligatory adverbials
lessons.meta: Some verbs need location or similar information to complete the clause
examples: She put the keys on the table.
The meeting lasted for two hours.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: put normally requires a destination; the place adverbial cannot simply be omitted.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The duration completes the meaning of lasted here.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: When residence location is the point, the place information completes the message.

rules: When put means placing something somewhere, it requires a place or direction adverbial after the object.
A duration prepositional phrase that completes a durative meaning is still an adverbial, not a direct object.
Obligatoriness may depend on verb valency and on what the context needs to express.

questions.question: What is “on the table” in “She put the keys on the table”?
questions.correct: It supplies the location required by put.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: It supplies the location required by put.

questions.question: What does “for two hours” express?
questions.correct: The prepositional phrase gives duration.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: The prepositional phrase gives duration.

questions.question: What mainly distinguishes an obligatory adverbial from an optional one?

options.text: The structure or meaning becomes incomplete

questions.correct: The key is whether it completes information required by the verb or context.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: The key is whether it completes information required by the verb or context.

narration.text: 有些地点、时长信息只是锦上添花，有些却是动词把意思说完整时少不了的一块。<#0.6#>She put the keys on the table。<#0.8#>put 表示把东西放到某处。the keys 说明放了什么，on the table 说明放到哪里。只听到“她把钥匙放了”，你会自然追问放在哪儿，所以这个地点信息在当前用法里是必需的。<#0.8#>The meeting lasted for two hours。<#0.6#>for two hours 给出会议持续的时长。这里不是动作指向一个宾语，而是 lasted 需要时长信息把“持续多久”交代清楚。<#0.8#>再看 He lives in Shanghai。<#0.6#>in Shanghai 说明居住地点。live 在这里表达“居住”，地点和动词的意义紧密相连；它虽然形式上是介词短语，却不能只因为带介词就随手删掉。<#0.8#>判断必要状语，不能只看它在句末，也不能只看它是不是介词短语。先找谓语，再暂时拿走后面的地点或时长信息。如果拿走后，听者一定会追问“放哪儿、持续多久、住哪儿”，这部分就是骨架所需的必要状语。

lessons.title: Linking verbs and transitivity
lessons.meta: Judge a verb by how it functions in context

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: smell links flowers with sweet and is a linking verb.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: smelled means actively sensed and takes an object.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: opened is intransitive here; compare She opened the door.

rules: A linking verb is followed by an element describing or identifying the subject, not receiving an action.
The same sense verb may be linking or transitive; inspect how the following element relates to the subject.
Many verbs can be transitive or intransitive; the pattern depends on the current use.

questions.question: What kind of verb is smell in “The flowers smell sweet”?
questions.correct: sweet describes the flowers.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: sweet describes the flowers.

questions.question: What is the pattern of “She smelled the flowers”?
questions.correct: the flowers is the object of smelled.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: the flowers is the object of smelled.

questions.question: What is the pattern of “The door opened”?
questions.correct: opened takes no object here.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: opened takes no object here.

narration.text: 同一个动词长得一样，在不同句子里却可能承担完全不同的任务，不能给它贴一张永久标签。<#0.6#>The flowers smell sweet。<#0.8#>这里不是花朵主动去闻什么，sweet 描写的是 flowers 的气味状态。smell 只把主语和这种状态连起来，所以它是系动词，句子是主系表。<#0.8#>再看 She smelled the flowers。<#0.6#>这次 She 做出“闻”的动作，动作直接指向 the flowers。smelled 成了及物动词，the flowers 是宾语，骨架也变成主谓宾。<#0.8#>The door opened。<#0.6#>opened 后面没有宾语，却已经说清“门开了”。门是发生变化的对象，但在句子结构里它是主语；opened 在这里是不及物用法，骨架是主谓。<#0.8#>所以判句型要从当前句子取证。先问动词是在连接主语的状态，还是在表达动作；如果是动作，再问它有没有直接指向的对象。关系变了，句型也会跟着变。

lessons.title: SVOO or SVOC?
lessons.meta: Ask whether the last two elements transfer or describe

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: me receives a message, so this is SVOO.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Leo and the baby refer to the same entity, so Leo is an object complement.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: difficult describes the task; it is not a second transferred object.

rules: The last two elements in SVOO are usually recipient plus thing: “to whom” and “what”.
In SVOC, the final element identifies, names or describes the object.
Do not classify solely because two elements follow the verb; test their semantic relationship.

questions.question: Which pattern is “She sent me a message”?
questions.correct: me is the recipient and message the thing.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: me is the recipient and message the thing.

questions.question: What is “Leo” in “They named the baby Leo”?
questions.correct: Leo names the baby.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: Leo names the baby.

questions.question: What is the best way to distinguish SVOO and SVOC?

options.text: Check whether the final elements show transfer or description
Only count the words after the verb

questions.correct: The relationship is more reliable than the surface word count.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: The relationship is more reliable than the surface word count.

narration.text: 动词后面连续出现两块内容，不代表一定是双宾语。真正要看的是：后两块是在完成一次传递，还是后一块在说明前一块。<#0.6#>She sent me a message。<#0.8#>sent 表示传递。a message 是被发送的内容，me 是接收的人。“给谁，加上什么”组成双宾语，所以骨架是主谓双宾。<#0.8#>They named the baby Leo。<#0.6#>这里没有两样东西被命名。the baby 是动作指向的宾语，Leo 说明这个宝宝被取了什么名字。Leo 和 the baby 是说明与被说明的关系，因此 Leo 是宾语补语，骨架是主谓宾补。<#0.8#>We found the task difficult。<#0.6#>the task 是发现所涉及的对象，difficult 描写这个任务呈现出的状态。它也不是接收者和事物，而是“宾语怎么样”。<#0.8#>判断时别数词，直接测试关系。能问“给谁、给什么”，后两项彼此独立，是双宾语；后一项在说明这个宾语是谁或怎么样，就是宾补。

lessons.title: Modifiers do not change the skeleton
lessons.meta: Temporarily set modifiers aside before classifying
examples: The girl with a red bag smiled warmly.
The book that you lent me is useful.
Yesterday, Tom quickly finished his homework.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: with a red bag postmodifies girl and warmly gives manner; neither changes the skeleton The girl smiled.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: that you lent me as a whole postmodifies book and has its own internal skeleton; the main clause remains The book is useful.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Yesterday and quickly add time and manner; removing them leaves the SVO skeleton Tom finished his homework.

rules: A postmodifying prepositional phrase belongs inside a noun phrase and adds no main-clause core slot.
A relative clause has its own internal skeleton but functions as a noun modifier in the main clause.
Movable or removable time and manner adverbials normally leave the basic skeleton unchanged.

questions.question: What is the main skeleton of “The girl with a red bag smiled warmly”?
questions.correct: with a red bag is a postmodifier and warmly an adverbial.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: with a red bag is a postmodifier and warmly an adverbial.

questions.question: What is the main-clause pattern of “The book that you lent me is useful”?
questions.correct: The main skeleton is The book is useful.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: The main skeleton is The book is useful.

questions.question: What remains after removing the adverbials from “Yesterday, Tom quickly finished his homework”?
questions.correct: Yesterday and quickly do not occupy core slots.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: Yesterday and quickly do not occupy core slots.

narration.text: 句子一长，最容易把所有词都算进基本句型。更稳的办法，是先把修饰信息轻轻拿开，看看核心关系还剩什么。<#0.6#>The girl with a red bag smiled warmly。<#0.8#>with a red bag 帮我们认出是哪一个 girl，warmly 说明笑的方式。真正的骨架只有 girl 和 smiled，是主谓结构；定语、状语再长，也不增加新的核心槽位。<#0.8#>The book that you lent me is useful。<#0.6#>that you lent me 整体跟在 book 后面，限定是哪本书。主句真正说的是这本书“是有用的”，is 连接主语和 useful，所以外层骨架是主系表。<#0.8#>Yesterday, Tom quickly finished his homework。<#0.6#>Yesterday 是时间，quickly 是方式；它们都在补充 finished。his homework 才是动作直接指向的宾语，核心骨架是主谓宾。<#0.8#>操作时按顺序做：先找完整谓语；再圈出它必需的主语、宾语或补语；最后把时间、地点、方式和名词旁的修饰语挂回去。修饰语让画面更具体，却不会凭空创造新句型。

lessons.title: Negatives, questions, passives and the skeleton
lessons.meta: The form changes, but participant relations can still be traced
examples: The door was opened by Tom.

exampleNotes.title: Transformation focus
exampleNotes.body: does carries finiteness, not marks negation, and the lexical verb like still governs coffee.

exampleNotes.title: Transformation focus
exampleNotes.body: Auxiliary inversion forms the question; restore statement order to see Tom opened the door.

exampleNotes.title: Transformation focus
exampleNotes.body: was and opened form the passive predicate; the active object becomes the current subject and by Tom marks the agent.

rules: Negation adds a negative element to the predicate; it does not turn an object into a complement.
Question inversion changes surface order; restore statement order when identifying the skeleton.
Passivisation changes grammatical positions; label the current sentence while tracing semantic links to the active.

narration.text: 句子变成否定、疑问或被动以后，单词位置和动词形式会变化，但谁和谁发生关系，仍然能追踪。<#0.6#>She does not like coffee。<#0.8#>does 和 not 帮助构成否定，真正表达“喜欢”的是 like，coffee 仍是这个动作直接涉及的宾语。因此加入否定，没有把主谓宾骨架变掉。<#0.8#>Did Tom open the door？<#0.6#>Did 被提前，用来发问；open 还原成原形。判断时要把 Did 和 open 合起来看成完整谓语，Tom 仍是主语，the door 仍是宾语。疑问语序不能把三个关系打乱。<#0.8#>The door was opened by Tom。<#0.6#>被动句把承受动作的 the door 放到主语位置，was opened 是完整谓语；by Tom 补出动作执行者。这里要按句子当前结构判断，而不是只看中文里谁做事。<#0.8#>遇到转换句，先找助动词和主要动词组成的完整谓语，再追问当前主语是谁、动作指向谁。形式变化是外壳，核心关系才是判型证据。

lessons.title: One verb, multiple patterns
lessons.meta: Do not assign a verb one permanent pattern

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: ring is intransitive here, forming SV.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: ring is transitive here, forming SVO.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: sound is linking here, forming SVC.

rules: ring is intransitive and forms SV when it means that a bell sounds with no object.
ring is transitive and forms SVO when it directly governs the thing caused to ring.
sound is a linking verb and forms SVC when followed by an element describing the subject.

questions.correct: rang takes no object here.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: rang takes no object here.

questions.correct: the bell is the object of rang.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: the bell is the object of rang.

questions.correct: sounds is linking and reasonable describes the idea.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: sounds is linking and reasonable describes the idea.

narration.text: 查到一个动词时，不能顺手在旁边写上“它永远属于某个句型”。句型属于整个句子，不属于一个孤零零的单词。<#0.6#>The bell rang。<#0.8#>rang 表示铃响了，后面不需要对象，意思已经完整，所以这里是不及物用法，骨架是主谓。<#0.8#>She rang the bell。<#0.6#>这次是她按响或摇响了铃。动作直接指向 the bell，rang 变成及物用法，the bell 是宾语，骨架是主谓宾。词形几乎没变，搭配关系已经变了。<#0.8#>The idea sounds reasonable。<#0.6#>sounds 不是“发出声音给某个对象”，而是把 The idea 和 reasonable 连起来，说明这个想法听起来合理。reasonable 描写主语，因此 sounds 在这里是系动词，骨架是主系表。<#0.8#>判断时每次都从零开始：先看动词在当前语境表达动作还是连接状态；再看后面是否有动作直接指向的对象。句内关系才是答案。

lessons.title: Coordinated predicates and shared elements
lessons.meta: Coordination does not always create multiple full clauses
examples: Tom opened the door and walked in.
Mia washed and dried the dishes.
Leo gave Amy a pen and a notebook.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The two predicates share Tom as subject; the second need not repeat it.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: washed and dried share the object the dishes.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Two direct objects are coordinated; the predicate and indirect object are shared.

rules: Coordinated predicates may share one subject; two verbs do not necessarily make two full clauses.
Coordinated verbs may share an object; identify which equal-level elements the conjunction links.
Objects themselves may be coordinated; a shared element appears once but relates to each relevant verb.

questions.correct: Both predicates share Tom.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: Both predicates share Tom.

questions.question: What does “the dishes” relate to in “Mia washed and dried the dishes”?
questions.correct: Both coordinated verbs share the object.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: Both coordinated verbs share the object.

questions.question: What is coordinated in “Leo gave Amy a pen and a notebook”?
questions.correct: a pen and a notebook are both direct objects.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: a pen and a notebook are both direct objects.

narration.text: 看到句子里有 and 和两个动词，不要马上宣布“这里有两个完整分句”。并列成分常常会共用前面已经出现的信息。<#0.6#>Tom opened the door and walked in。<#0.8#>opened 和 walked in 都由 Tom 发出，第二个动作没有再写一个主语。这里是同一个主语带两个并列谓语，不是两个各自写全主语的分句。<#0.8#>Mia washed and dried the dishes。<#0.6#>washed 和 dried 不但共用主语 Mia，还共用后面的 the dishes。碗碟同时是“洗”和“擦干”所涉及的对象，不能只把它连给离得最近的 dried。<#0.8#>Leo gave Amy a pen and a notebook。<#0.6#>这次 and 连接的不是两个谓语，而是 a pen 和 a notebook 两个直接宾语。它们共用 gave 和接收者 Amy。<#0.8#>判断并列时，先看 and 两边形式相当的是什么，再把省略信息补到脑中。连词连接哪一级，句子就在哪一级并列；动词多，不等于分句一定多。

lessons.title: Integrated pattern identification
lessons.meta: Predicate first, required elements next, modifiers last
examples: The children became quiet after lunch.
Our teacher showed us an interesting video.
The joke kept everyone awake all night.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: quiet describes the children and after lunch is temporal; the skeleton is SVC.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: us is the recipient and the video the content shown, giving SVOO.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: awake describes everyone and all night is adverbial, giving SVOC.

rules: First decide whether the predicate is an action verb or linking verb, then identify what follows.
When two postverbal elements mean recipient plus thing, they form indirect and direct objects.
Cross-check with relations such as describing the subject, receiving an action, receiving a thing or describing the object.

questions.correct: became is linking and quiet is a subject complement.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: became is linking and quiet is a subject complement.

questions.correct: us receives the video, forming two objects.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: us receives the video, forming two objects.

questions.correct: awake describes the object everyone.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: awake describes the object everyone.

narration.text: 综合判型时，不靠“看起来像”，而是沿着固定路线找证据：先谓语，再必需成分，最后排除修饰语。<#0.6#>The children became quiet after lunch。<#0.8#>became 表示状态变化，quiet 描写 children 变得怎么样；after lunch 只交代时间。因此核心是主语、系动词和表语，也就是 SVC。<#0.8#>Our teacher showed us an interesting video。<#0.6#>showed 表示展示，an interesting video 是展示的内容，us 是接收内容的人。“给谁看什么”形成两个宾语，所以骨架是 SVOO。<#0.8#>The joke kept everyone awake all night。<#0.6#>everyone 是 kept 直接涉及的对象，awake 说明 everyone 保持什么状态；all night 只补充持续时长。后两项是“宾语怎么样”，所以 awake 是宾补，骨架是 SVOC。<#0.8#>三句表面都在动词后带了不止一块内容，但关系不同。先拿走时间等状语，再问后面的成分是在说明主语、完成传递，还是说明宾语。

lessons.title: Boundaries of basic sentence patterns
lessons.meta: Patterns describe the main skeleton; clause types are analysed separately
examples: I know that she is right.
The girl who won is my sister.

exampleNotes.title: Boundary note
exampleNotes.body: The main clause is SVO; the object clause has its own internal SVC skeleton.

exampleNotes.title: Boundary note
exampleNotes.body: The subject clause occupies the subject slot as a whole; the main skeleton is still SVO.

exampleNotes.title: Boundary note
exampleNotes.body: who won has an internal SV skeleton but as a whole only postmodifies girl; the main skeleton is The girl is my sister.

rules: A basic pattern describes the core arrangement within a clause; it is not the same as simple, compound or complex sentence classification.
A nominal clause can fill a subject, object or complement slot and has its own internal pattern.
Relative and adverbial clauses are modifying clause types, not additional basic sentence patterns.

questions.correct: The object clause as a whole is the object of know.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: The object clause as a whole is the object of know.

questions.correct: The subject clause fills the subject slot.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: The subject clause fills the subject slot.

questions.correct: It postmodifies girl and is not a basic pattern category.
questions.wrong: Check the sentence skeleton: It postmodifies girl and is not a basic pattern category.

narration.text: 基本句型只描述一个分句的核心骨架，并不等于把整句贴成“简单句、复合句”这些类别。句子里有从句时，要先看它整体占什么位置，再进到内部分析。<#0.6#>I know that she is right。<#0.8#>主句里 I 是主语，know 是谓语，that she is right 整体回答“知道什么”，占宾语位置，所以主句骨架是 SVO。从句内部还有自己的结构，但不能和外层混着数。<#0.8#>What he said surprised me。<#0.6#>What he said 虽然内部有多个词，却整体站在 surprised 前，承担主语；me 是宾语。外层仍是 SVO。先框出从句边界，比逐词抢位置更重要。<#0.8#>The girl who won is my sister。<#0.6#>who won 跟在 girl 后面，帮助确定是哪位女孩，整体作后置定语。主句中 is 连接 The girl 和 my sister，所以外层是 SVC。<#0.8#>遇到复杂句，先用括号把从句当成一个大块，判断它在外层是主语、宾语还是修饰语；完成主句判型后，再进入从句内部。这是两张不同的地图。
